title: Evaluate prompt lookup as cheaper speculation - execution and acceptance
protocol: offload --moe-cache-auto --max-running-requests 1, kv nvfp4 220032; plain vs --lookup-draft 4 --lookup-ngram 6 --lookup-min-ngram 2; 128 greedy decode; fixtures rep1k/rep4k (repeated passage) and prose16k (03b fixture)

cases.detail: lookup changed the greedy output sha on prose16k (00082e945c2c vs f8cb8d6f5b7b) -> spurious min_ngram matches drafted
lookup is slower on every workload (-11% to -44%), including repetitive text where drafts should win

decision.reason: draft-free PLD regresses decode on this PCIe-bound offload box: the multi-token verify frame and graph changes cost more than the saved decode steps even on repetitive text, and weak matches alter the greedy output. Keep lookup_draft=0 (default).

rollback_recipe: n/a (no production change; lookup is opt-in and stays off)
limitations: Single configuration (depth 4, max_ngram 6, min_ngram 2); other depths not swept.
greedy + CUDA graphs on (max bs 1); the spec frame changes graph shapes.
Repetitive fixtures are synthetic repeats of one passage.
